newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 17.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Bangladesh will open diplomatic missions in the Maldives, Jordan and Brunei.
Italy will provide $10 million as soft loan to implement four projects in Bangladesh.
South Asian experts have termed arsenic contamination of ground water in Bangladesh a major public health hazard, and called on the government to tackle it on emergency basis.
The government on Wednesday asked shops to close by 7 pm in the wake of shortfall in electricity generation.
The newly appointed chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission, Abu Sayeed, took over the charge on Wednesday.
A new industrial policy will be placed in the next session of the parliament for approval.
Bangladesh and Saipan will sign a bilateral agreement next month on exporting opf manpower to the island country.
The World Bank lending to South Asia fell about $1 billion short of its commitment in the fiscal 1996-97. REUTER
